title: mcp-trace-validator baseline
description: The findings an author has accepted, for `mcp-trace-validator validate --baseline` (ADR-0025): each is named by the fingerprint SARIF reports for it (`partialFingerprints["mcpConformanceFinding/v2"]`), with the reason it is accepted and, optionally, the last day it is. `validate --write-baseline` writes one. Closed (`additionalProperties: false`), as the reader is: an unknown member would otherwise be ignored in silence. The reader also rejects what a schema cannot say: a `reason` with no non-blank character, a repeated `fingerprint`, and an `expires` that is not a day on the calendar.

version.description: The version of this file format.

fingerprint_key.description: The scheme the fingerprints are of: the key SARIF reports them under. A build that computes another scheme refuses the file, and does not call every entry stale.

findings.description: The accepted findings. Written sorted by fingerprint, so a diff of the file shows only what changed.

fingerprint.description: The finding's identity: `{rule}:{check}:{detail with digit runs folded to #}:{n}`. It carries no `seq` and no trace path, so a re-recorded or renamed trace keeps it; it changes with a finding's wording (a renamed tool), a check's name, and a release that rewords either. Unique in the file.

reason.description: Why the finding is accepted, in words. Must contain a non-blank character. `--write-baseline` writes a sentence saying the finding was recorded and not reviewed (`baseline::GENERATED_REASON`), and every run counts how many entries still carry it.

expires.description: The last day (UTC) the entry accepts the finding, `YYYY-MM-DD`. From the next day the entry accepts nothing and the finding counts again; the report names the lapsed entry.
